newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Czech MP to back govt if house links key selloffs.
newsitem.headline: Czech MP to back govt if house links key selloffs.

text.p: Independent Czech parliamentary deputy Jozef Wagner, whose support may be important for government to win a confidence vote, said on Tuesday he would back the cabinet if it allows a vote on certain banking and utility privatisations.

"I am willing to (vote for the cabinet) only under the condition that the prime minister declares...that the chamber of deputies (lower house) decides on the concept of the potential privatisation of infrastructure and banks, and that without approval of this chamber no further concrete steps are made," Wagner told the house.

Czech Prime Minister Vaclav Klaus earlier on Tuesday called for a vote of confidence in his embattled cabinet and its programme to tackle economic ills including sagging confidence in the Czech crown.
"If Mr. Prime Minister declares this, I will support the government in this (confidence) vote," Wagner added.

Wagner rejected opposition claims that the government's planned privatisations of key banks and energy distributors should ensure they are kept in Czech hands, and said the country should look abroad for capital and know-how.
But he said the house should be allowed a vote on the questions.

Wagner is the chairman of the house budget committee who was expelled from the opposition Social Democrats after he voted with the government and gave Prime Minister Vaclav Klaus a narrow victory in approving the 1997 budget late last year.

Analysts expect at least 97 opposition deputies to vote against the government, but the votes of the two unaffiliated deputies are still not clear and one deputy from the Communist party has said he is unable to vote for health reasons.

The finance ministry last week announced plans to sell off key stakes in two of the largest commercial banks Komercni Banka a.s. and Ceskoslovenska Obchodni Banka a.s. and in 18 gas and electricity distributors.
At the beginning of the Czech post-Communist transformation earlier this decade, parliament granted final say over privatisation decisions to the cabinet.
